emerging_technology: Large-language-model generative AI used by human analysts for bilingual synthesis, public-source market/competitor research and draft market-entry recommendations; no autonomous purchases, negotiation or fieldwork.
industry_sector: Small cross-border management/market-entry consulting practices serving Chinese home/lifestyle consumer brands considering the U.S. market.
users_stakeholders: Chinese brand founders and export/marketing teams; bilingual analysts; U.S. consumers and research participants; channel partners; consulting principals and affected junior staff.
adoption_posture: Moderate / fast follower: consider a reversible, human-reviewed pilot before changing client commitments or staffing.
risk_consequence_context: Incorrect or stale market advice can misallocate client budgets and damage trust; cross-cultural errors, unsupported sources, confidential data leakage and misleading claims are material. No legal/tax/customs/product-compliance advice; refer those decisions to qualified professionals. Management retains approval.
management_question: Over the next 12 months, should management absorb LLM generative AI as an analyst productivity tool, change the paid value proposition, or do both? What evidence would justify the next step?
time_horizon: Decision as of October 13, 2026. Proposed explicit analytical windows: near = now through October 13, 2027; mid = after that through October 13, 2029; far = beyond October 13, 2029. These scenario conventions are not chapter-defined cutoffs or forecasts.
additional_context:
Selected by the student: generative AI and small consultancies helping Chinese consumer brands enter the United States. This is a hypothetical organization-type case, not a study of an identified real firm. All organization attributes below are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured facts. No private client data or invented interviews are supplied. Product category: non-food home/lifestyle consumer goods; exclude regulated-product recommendations and legal, tax, customs or product-compliance advice. Reference date: October 13, 2026. General evidence snapshot must remain fixed across all three tests.
Verified conceptual source C1: Andres Fortino, Mastering the Craft of Emerging Technology Adoption, Chapter 1, August 2026 Rev 0.1 classroom draft; supplied by the student and read locally. Sections 1.2–1.6 distinguish sustaining/disruptive mechanisms, waves and the incumbent dilemma. Figure 1.8 p.11 provides Low/Moderate/High severity by near/mid/far horizon; High/near = act now, High/mid = prepare and pilot, High/far = monitor closely; Moderate/near = pilot or partner, Moderate/mid = monitor and build optionality, Moderate/far = note and revisit; Low/near = sustaining update, Low/mid = routine tracking, Low/far = disregard for now. C1 is a conceptual framework, not verified market evidence for this case.
External evidence limitation: cloud retrieval attempts on October 13, 2026 to https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161, https://www.hbs.edu/faculty/Pages/item.aspx?num=64700, https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/plan-your-business/market-research-competitive-analysis and https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf were blocked by the proxy with 403. No measured willingness-to-pay, churn, cost, margin, accuracy, U.S. market size or conversion data are available. If interactive ChatGPT has browsing, verify original sources and save the actual references and relevant limits; otherwise explicitly qualify/abstain on dependent claims. Do not treat Chinese-to-English fluency as proof of U.S. consumer validity or an AI-generated interview as a real interview. Distinguish a client self-service alternative hypothesis from observed displacement. Do not assume ownership of relationships creates an unassailable moat.
intended_application: Produce a paid bilingual U.S. market-entry research package: public-source competitor map, target-customer hypotheses, indicative channel options and a draft launch recommendation, all reviewed by a human consultant.
organization: Hypothetical small bilingual consultancy, report-led model: Chinese home/lifestyle brands pay fixed project fees for research packages. This is an explicit scenario, not an identified firm.
business_need: Protect the value of paid research while testing whether lower delivery cost can serve smaller brands that currently cannot afford bespoke work. Assess the hypothesis that clients can self-serve generic report content and reduce willingness to pay.
capabilities_constraints: Assumed baseline: junior analysts assemble public information; senior consultants review narrative and recommendations; reports and a presentation are the main deliverables. Limited proprietary consumer evidence and limited U.S. channel relationships. Project fees depend on scope, with no measured pricing or margins supplied. Client acquisition is through referrals and direct outreach. Claimed advantages are bilingual synthesis and structured advice; their defensibility is unverified. Pilot uses public or consented/redacted inputs, records sources and review time, and keeps human sign-off. No quantified time/cost savings are assumed.
